items.titulo: Daily Search Forum Recap: November 18, 2026
items.resumen: Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today...

items.titulo: Microsoft Rolls Out Its Biggest Bidding Upgrade In A Decade via @sejournal, @brookeosmundson
items.resumen: Microsoft Advertising is automatically updating its bidding models, reporting faster target adjustments, smoother budget pacing, and best practices for CPA and ROAS campaigns. The post Microsoft Rolls Out Its Biggest Bidding Upgrade In A Decade appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: Google Ads Releases Several AI Max For Search For Travel Campaigns Help Docs
items.resumen: Google has released several new Google Ads help documents on the topic of AI Max for Search for Travel campaigns. This comes as Google begins to migrate Travel campaigns to the new Search campaigns for Travel in Google Ads.

items.titulo: Win the holiday shopping season with November’s Demand Gen Drop.
items.resumen: Take advantage of the holiday peak with YouTube’s November Demand Gen Drop.

items.titulo: Google Ads AI Max Is Making More Decisions For You – Here’s What To Audit Now via @sejournal, @brookeosmundson
items.resumen: Audit Google Ads AI Max settings to catch unwanted searches, review generated ad copy, and keep landing pages aligned with campaign goals. The post Google Ads AI Max Is Making More Decisions For You – Here’s What To Audit Now appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: Google Ads New Commercial Exemptions To US Election Advertising Policy
items.resumen: Google Ads has added a new exemption to its political content policy for "Commercial exceptions to US Election Ads." This essentially exempts ads that feature candidates solely for government programs or commercial products, without political references, from US Election Ads verification.

items.titulo: Websites Aren’t Just For People Anymore. Here’s How Marketers Optimize Them For Agents
items.resumen: Knotch's new AI marketing solution focuses on making website content more accessible to AI agents, which improves brand discoverability in LLMs. The post Websites Aren’t Just For People Anymore. Here’s How Marketers Optimize Them For Agents appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Google Tag & Google Tag Manager Unification
items.resumen: This past August, Google announced the unification of Google tag and Google Tag Manager. Well, today Google posted a Google Tag Manager release not about the unification. It is titled Google tag and Google Tag Manager unification and dated on November 17, 2026.

items.titulo: Google's AI Mode cuts clicks to websites by 18.8 points, field test finds
items.resumen: Searchers put in AI Mode were 11.2 points likelier to use Bing, DuckDuckGo or Yahoo. What a March test of 1,100 US users cannot tell publishers or advertisers.

items.titulo: Microsoft Advertising Announces Biggest Upgrade To Bidding Models
items.resumen: Microsoft announced the "biggest upgrade" to bidding models in a decade within Microsoft Advertising. Microsoft wrote, "we're continuously listening to customer feedback to understand the ways we can make our bidding deliver better results for advertisers, and now we're rolling out the biggest upgrade to bidding models in a decade."

items.titulo: Google Ads Surcharges Rise To 3% In France And Italy – Local US Advertisers Can Be Billed Too via @sejournal, @gregjarboe
items.resumen: Check where your Google Ads run: default location settings can expose local campaigns to surcharges in France and Italy. The post Google Ads Surcharges Rise To 3% In France And Italy – Local US Advertisers Can Be Billed Too appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: Meta Ads Promotions and Email Sign-up Offers: What They Do and How to Turn Them Off
items.resumen: Meta ads promotions can show promo codes on your ads automatically. Learn how they and email sign-up offers work and how to turn them off. The post Meta Ads Promotions and Email Sign-up Offers: What They Do and How to Turn Them Off appeared first on Jon Loomer Digital .

items.titulo: Trade Desk picks Attain, with 15 million consumers, to anchor ad measurement
items.resumen: Open Measurement launches later this quarter, judging publishers' media by purchases rather than last clicks. Can a DSP's own yardstick stay neutral for brands?

items.titulo: Philips Sonicare Polishes Its Streaming TV Strategy Using Amazon Ads Agent
items.resumen: Philips Sonicare, a maker of electric toothbrushes and water flossers, decided to consolidate its streaming TV ad buys within Amazon, which has also been doing some consolidating itself. The post Philips Sonicare Polishes Its Streaming TV Strategy Using Amazon Ads Agent appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Unsupported Google tag installs get the Tag Manager upgrade in January 2027
items.resumen: Google tag users now reach Tag Assistant data through GTM container permissions, and new snippets drop gtag config. What changes on websites, and what stays?

items.titulo: California fines Hertz $1.55m over unprocessed browser opt-out signals
items.resumen: Trackers from Meta, Google, TikTok and 10 other ad tech firms ran while Hertz sites missed GPC opt-outs. Now every tag gets tested each quarter until 2029.

items.titulo: Search interest rises 18% when brands return to TV after a year off, VAB says
items.resumen: Website visitors rose 57% for 11 brands as returning advertisers doubled TV budgets to $4.9m. Without a control group, did the screen or the money do the work?

items.titulo: 6.9% Of ChatGPT Conversations Showed Purchase Intent In U.S. Panel via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.resumen: U.S. data finds few ChatGPT conversations show intent to buy and most responses name no brand. New insight for teams weighing ChatGPT visibility and ads. The post 6.9% Of ChatGPT Conversations Showed Purchase Intent In U.S. Panel appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: California sues OpenAI over escaped agents as Google's AI Mode cuts clicks
items.resumen: California sued OpenAI over AI agents that escaped testing, a field study found AI Mode cuts clicks by 18.8 points, and Amazon rewrote its gambling ad rules.

items.titulo: Temu faces EU fine of up to 6% over checks on unsafe products
items.resumen: Sanctions hit single Temu stores, not the traders running several, and test reports often go unchecked, Brussels says. What comes before any fine is decided?

items.titulo: CNIL fines unnamed life insurer €5m over 1.8m passwords stored in plain text
items.resumen: 1.3m policyholders' records sat behind one shared login. The fine, sized on its group's premiums, fell from a €9m proposal. Why is the insurer left unnamed?

items.titulo: EDPB picks AI candidate screening as its 2027 enforcement target
items.resumen: Screening tools that reject job candidates without a human will be tested on Article 22 and access rights. Which DPAs join, and what changes for Korea data?

items.titulo: Booking's parent and Agoda must face €965m Dutch consumer claim
items.resumen: Agoda's Singapore court clause did not bind the foundation suing for Dutch hotel guests. The claim also wants A/B test logs and source code. Will judges agree?

items.titulo: News takes 32% of Latin American podcast listening, Triton finds
items.resumen: Prisa Radio leads LATAM podcast networks with 2.47m weekly downloads, and news fills 42% of new episodes. Is day-one audio worth the premium Triton claims?

items.titulo: Opera loses 5 million users but earns 22% more from each one
items.resumen: Advertising rose 22% to $116.8m and query revenue 17% to $65.0m, while e-commerce ads cooled under new EU rules. Can gaming and CTV ads carry Opera into 2027?

items.titulo: Similarweb books first GAAP profit as AI-related sales near 20% of revenue
items.resumen: AI-related deals made two-thirds of Q3's new ARR while accounts over $25k fell to 1,790. Can growth hold as a new CEO runs a business that sells data to AI?

items.titulo: Google AI Overviews With Unfaded Citation Block
items.resumen: Google seems to have rolled out an update to the AI Overviews on the Google Search page where the citation cards or blocks on the right side are not faded out. Instead, the citations are fully visible, and you don't need to click into the AI Overview to view them fully.

items.titulo: Google lists six ways sites still block its AI agent after allowing it
items.resumen: Shared IPs, in-page CAPTCHAs and add-to-cart calls trip up Google-Agent at site firewalls. Robots.txt generally does not apply, so what control do sites keep?

items.titulo: New Google Search Help Document On How To Allow Google-Agent Traffic
items.resumen: Google released a new help document on how to allow Google-Agent to have access to your website. "Google-Agent is the name used by agents hosted on Google infrastructure to navigate the web and perform actions upon user request," the document says.

items.titulo: Google Tests Sign In Protections After First Search To Block Scrapers
items.resumen: Google has been testing numerous ways to block scrapers and third-party tools from crawling its search results page. The latest effort seems to require a user to sign in immediately after the first search. But Rajan Patel from Google said on X that he will look into this but "I don't believe it's meant to happen on the first page of results like this but we may be testing something here..."

items.titulo: Gemini's $19.99 task mode goes free in 6 countries
items.resumen: US users also get AI calls to businesses in all but 5 states and card payments through Visa and Mastercard tokens. Will websites let the agent finish the job?

items.titulo: Character.ai faces a privacy ombudsman before its users' data can be sold
items.resumen: Its report is due 7 days before any sale hearing and goes under seal to states, creditors and the debtor first. Who decides if chats count as personal data?

items.titulo: FBI ties SEO poisoning on hacked WordPress sites to $28 million in ransoms
items.resumen: Gootloader aimed at lawyers through low-competition legal searches and 216 domains. The FBI wants site owners watching Search Console for unrelated queries.

items.titulo: FBI: SEO Poisoning Led To $28 Million In Ransomware Payments
items.resumen: The FBI, Federal Bureau of Investigation, has a newsletter named the FBI FLASH, and in the November 16th edition, it highlighted SEO poisoning through Gootloader malware. This resulted in "over 1000 infected WordPress sites and 216 domains controlled by the Gootloader administrator, which led to over $28 million in ransomware payments," the FBI said.

items.titulo: Putting AI To Work At WSJ
items.resumen: The best AI use cases in ad sales aren’t flashy. Mostly, it’s about automating the tasks nobody wanted to do anyway. That’s been the case at The Wall Street Journal, where AI is quietly taking over most of the busywork for the ad sales team, says Josh Stinchcomb, the Journal’s global CRO, on this week’s […] The post Putting AI To Work At WSJ appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Canvas Worldwide’s Agentic Layer Helps Zillow Distinguish Real Renters From Dreamers
items.resumen: Canvas' AI solutions help brands and agencies like Zillow optimize their campaign budgeting and pacing. The post Canvas Worldwide’s Agentic Layer Helps Zillow Distinguish Real Renters From Dreamers appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Google: A Site Move Doesn't Improve A Site's Overall Quality
items.resumen: John Mueller from Google said that simply moving a site to a new domain does not improve a site's overall quality. He wrote this on Bluesky, "A site move doesn't improve the site's overall quality." I mean, this is pretty obvious, but sometimes I like to cover the obvious.

items.titulo: Google On Why Serving A 200 Status Code When Your Site Is Down Is Bad
items.resumen: Google's John Mueller posted two reasons why it would be bad to serve a 200 status code to Googlebot when your site or web pages are down. He said that if your site is down and the page says an error message, that message will be shown in the Google Search results and also, if the same text is on all your pages, Google can de-duplicate the pages and your pages can drop out of the index.

items.titulo: Daily Search Forum Recap: November 17, 2026
items.resumen: Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today, through the eyes of the Search Engine Roundtable and other search forums on the web. The FBI posted an alert about SEO poisoning through malware. Moving a site does not and should not improve a site's quality...

items.titulo: Game: Diaspora viewers are the most underpriced seats on the sofa
items.resumen: Sixteen terms in four groups for Thursday. One set comes from this week's coverage, and several tiles pretend to be gadget brands they never were.

items.titulo: One Meta ad can now carry up to 5 existing posts
items.resumen: Each person sees the post Meta predicts they will engage with, so advertisers promoting organic posts hand Meta the pick. Will reports show how each post did?

items.titulo: Google Ads PMax Setup Now With Channel Prioritization & Promo Mode
items.resumen: Google Ads has added two features to the Performance Max campaign set up screen for Channel Prioritization and Promo Mode. While Channel Prioritization and Promo Mode are not new, it is reportedly new within this campaign set up screen.

items.titulo: Google Hotel Campaigns Migrating To Search Campaigns For Travel
items.resumen: While Google is migrating travel campaigns to the Search campaigns for Travel now, Google will be migrating Hotel campaigns will or is migrating to new Search campaigns for Travel this quarter, Q4 2026.

items.titulo: New Google Ads Search Journey Awareness Help Document
items.resumen: Google Ads posted a new help document named About Search Journey Awareness. Journey-Aware Bidding is not new, but I believe this help document is new. Google explained, "Search Journey Awareness is an improvement to Google Ads Smart Bidding."

items.titulo: Google Ads Brand Guidelines New Add Visual Guidelines
items.resumen: Google Ads added a new option under the brand guidelines for Performance Max campaigns to add visual guidelines. This says, "Now you can add style references and preferences to help steer how images are created and enhanced for your ads."

items.titulo: Google Local Services Ads Historical Reports Can Now Be Downloaded
items.resumen: You can now download your historical Google Local Services Ads reports on the redirection page of Google Local Services Ads. Previously, Google said the download feature was coming and now Google said it is finally here.

items.titulo: Google adds Oklahoma and Alabama to its ad privacy tools, now 24 states
items.resumen: Alabama's law starts May 1, 2027, 120 days after Google's date, while Ad Manager reads just five state GPP sections. Which states get browser opt-outs next?

items.titulo: Disney will stop reporting streaming profit after an 11.5% margin year
items.resumen: Ad sales reached $11.5bn, up 4%, but lower rates cut Entertainment ad growth by 5 points. A free Disney+ tier under study would add more inventory to sell.

items.titulo: Meta Makes Its Way To The Big(ish) Screen; Fubo’s Fraught Q3
items.resumen: MeT∀ YouTube has become TV, video podcasts are following suit and now Meta is looking for its way into the living room. Meta has already been testing Instagram for TV built around long-form creator content. But it could make a bigger splash in the TV world through the acquisition of a CTV startup or a […] The post Meta Makes Its Way To The Big(ish) Screen; Fubo’s Fraught Q3 appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: FuboTV drops quarterly subscriber reporting at 5.75 million
items.resumen: Ad sales rose 22% to $119.1 million on Disney's ad server, while North American subscribers fell by 260,000 in a year. What will advertisers track instead?

items.titulo: Stop Hunting for Hang-Gliding Nuns. Your Local CTV Campaign Needs Scale.
items.resumen: Premion’s Head of Pricing and Planning, Adolfo Arbulú, on why hyper-targeting suffocates local CTV campaigns, and why AI still requires a human in the lead. It is easy to get seduced by the promise of hyper-targeting in connected TV. But stacking audience filters—like trying to reach “hang-gliding nuns who drink energy drinks”—creates a massive problem […] The post Stop Hunting for Hang-Gliding Nuns. Your Local CTV Campaign Needs Scale. appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Disney Touts Its Streaming Success In Latest Earnings
items.resumen: After a lot of internal upheaval and consolidation, the House of Mouse finds itself in a pretty good place going into its fiscal 2027 year. The post Disney Touts Its Streaming Success In Latest Earnings appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: AdTonos drops its name after 10 years to chase in-car ads as Turms
items.resumen: Carmakers are pitched ad revenue from cars already on the road, as an AI buyer still in development picks if an ad runs. No carmaker or launch date is named.

items.titulo: Motorway ad seller i-media wins exclusive rights at Gridserve EV sites
items.resumen: Drivers wait 27 minutes on average at charging sites, i-media says, and finance, travel and luxury brands are its target. How does its number-plate data work?

items.titulo: Ad Tech Doesn’t Need Another Tool. It Needs Fewer Handoffs
items.resumen: Every few months, we get excited about an industry update, like a new ad format or AI tool. That energy is a big part of what keeps ad tech moving forward, but I believe the next five years will be shaped less by any single innovation and more by how well the tools we already […] The post Ad Tech Doesn’t Need Another Tool. It Needs Fewer Handoffs appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Only 2 of Amazon's 42 engagement metrics cover Sponsored Products
items.resumen: All 16 audio metrics serve DVA+ alone, and video benchmarks reach only Sponsored Brands advertisers. What does a completed view count, and against which peers?

items.titulo: Amazon limits daily unified reports to 120 days of its 24-month history
items.resumen: Sponsored Products video carries real data in only 2 metrics, and its other zeros are placeholders. Which report fields come back null, and from what date?

items.titulo: Amazon's Fire tablet ad impressions can arrive after a campaign ends
items.resumen: Advertisers get muted video of 15 seconds or less in the US, UK, Germany and Japan only, and review takes up to 12 hours. Why can reports move after the end?

items.titulo: JD.com cuts marketing spend 26% as food delivery losses halve
items.resumen: Marketplace and marketing revenue rose 9.6% to RMB28.1bn as brands lifted ad spend by double digits. Can AI-led search lift JD Retail's 5.8% margin in 2027?

items.titulo: Walmart's $35 meal for 10 gets 14 store-brand extras, all unpriced
items.resumen: Priced on a 13.5 lb turkey at $0.97 a pound, the basket meets ham, crab cakes and cheesecake picked by Walmart's own developers. What will the full table cost?
